question_text:
A 2-year-old boy presents with a swollen face and irritability. The patient's mother reports his urine was red this morning. 3 weeks ago, he presented to this same clinic with a ‘sandpaper’ rash and a red tongue with patchy hyperplastic fungiform papillae for which he was given broad-spectrum antibiotics. Laboratory tests reveal proteinuria, elevated antistreptolysin O, and decreased serum C3. Which of the following conditions mentioned below are triggered by a similar mechanism?
I. Arthus reaction
II. Myasthenia gravis
III. Acute rheumatic fever
IV. Polyarteritis nodosa
V. Rheumatoid arthritis?

                    ### Question
                    A 2-year-old boy presents with a swollen face and irritability. The patient's mother reports his urine was red this morning. 3 weeks ago, he presented to this same clinic with a ‘sandpaper’ rash and a red tongue with patchy hyperplastic fungiform papillae for which he was given broad-spectrum antibiotics. Laboratory tests reveal proteinuria, elevated antistreptolysin O, and decreased serum C3. Which of the following conditions mentioned below are triggered by a similar mechanism?
I. Arthus reaction
II. Myasthenia gravis
III. Acute rheumatic fever
IV. Polyarteritis nodosa
V. Rheumatoid arthritis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. I, II
opb. III, IV
opc. I, IV, V
opd. II, III, IV
ope. I, IV, V

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The 2-year-old boy's symptoms, including facial swelling, irritability, red urine, and laboratory findings of proteinuria, elevated antistreptolysin O, and decreased serum C3, are consistent with acute rheumatic fever (ARF), which is an autoimmune response following a streptococcal infection. ARF can trigger autoimmune mechanisms similar to those seen in Myasthenia gravis and rheumatoid arthritis. The Arthus reaction is a type III hypersensitivity reaction and is not related to the autoimmune mechanisms of ARF. Polyarteritis nodosa has a different pathophysiology and is not triggered by the same mechanisms as ARF. Therefore, the conditions triggered by a similar mechanism to ARF are Myasthenia gravis and rheumatoid arthritis. The best-supported option is III (acute rheumatic fever), II (Myasthenia gravis), and IV (rheumatoid arthritis).
